title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
event_hint: SAC (Sparse Attention on CXL): first CXL-based disaggregated KV cache system for sparse attention LLM serving (DeepSeek-V3.2 AWQ 4-bit on SGLang/HiSparse, 8-H20 GPU server with 2TB CXL memory pool).
problem: Traditional RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache pools (e.g., MoonCake, LMCache) full-fetch the entire prefix KV cache from remote to local memory before decoding. For sparse attention models (DeepSeek Sparse Attention, top-k=2048 per layer), only a small fraction of KV entries are active per layer, so full-fetching wastes transmission bandwidth (transmission bottleneck P1: long queuing delays and degraded TTFT/throughput at high client concurrency on 100 Gbps RNIC) and wastes local memory (P2: only 21% of KV cache utilized at 128K context; DeepSeek-V3.2 needs 9.2 GB/request at 128K, requiring TB-level local memory for high concurrency). RDMA's message-based send/recv semantics also impose per-request software-stack overhead that accumulates across all attention layers for fine-grained top-k reads, and during decode the RDMA path contends with the HiSparse swap-in process for PCIe bandwidth, raising TBT.
mechanism: SAC replaces RDMA with a CXL-based disaggregated KV cache pool exposing hardware-managed load/store semantics at cache-line granularity, accessed through a CXL switch (CXL 2.0/3.0, Type-3 memory devices). Built on the HiSparse framework inside SGLang, the decode instance computes top-k indices per attention layer at runtime and uses an optimized Swap-in CUDA kernel (miss identification + LRU eviction + page-table update + fetch) to fetch only the required top-k KV entries directly from the CXL memory pool into GPU HBM on demand; newly generated token KV is written back to CXL. The CXL system maps all KV data into a global CXL address space shared across compute instances, with device initialization, optimized read/write kernels, and device interleaving across multiple CXL memory devices (interleaving mitigates link-level contention and is shown to scale toward the local-DRAM bound). Prefill instance writes full KV blocks to the CXL pool after prefill. The HiSparse device_buffer_size (hot KV kept in GPU HBM) is a key tunable; a 6K buffer yields ~10.4% higher average throughput than a 4K buffer by lowering the KV miss rate.

evidence.claim: On DeepSeek-V3.2 (AWQ 4-bit) end-to-end serving via SGLang/HiSparse on an 8-H20 GPU server with a 2TB CXL memory pool, across context lengths 16K-128K (ShareGPT, 512 requests, 1K-token output, concurrency 64 in the decode/Cache-Hit round), SAC achieves on average 2.1x higher throughput, 9.7x lower TTFT and 1.8x lower TBT compared with an RDMA-based memory pool baseline.
evidence.value: 2.1x throughput; 9.7x lower TTFT; 1.8x lower TBT (Round-2 decode averages, 16K-128K context)
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 AWQ 4-bit on SGLang/HiSparse, 8x H20 GPU, 2TB CXL pool, ShareGPT 512 requests, 1K output, Round-2 concurrency 64, context 16K-128K
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 7 (Section 5, 5.1 End-to-End Performance Comparison, Figures 9-10)

evidence.claim: Across both prefill (Round-1) and decode (Round-2) rounds, SAC throughput stays within 91% of the local-DRAM upper bound with only marginal TBT/TTFT increase, i.e., about a 9% throughput degradation versus the non-disaggregated local-memory baseline.
evidence.value: ~9% throughput degradation vs local DRAM upper bound (throughput within 91% of DRAM)
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 AWQ 4-bit on SGLang/HiSparse, 8x H20 GPU, 2TB CXL pool, 16K-128K context, both rounds

evidence.claim: The 1.8x TBT penalty of the RDMA baseline relative to SAC is attributed to severe PCIe bus contention, since the PCIe bus must simultaneously handle incoming KV cache traffic and the HiSparse swap-in process; the 9.7x TTFT penalty is attributed to high client concurrency saturating transmission bandwidth during KV retrieval and increasing queuing delays.
evidence.value: RDMA TBT 1.8x vs SAC (PCIe contention); RDMA TTFT 9.7x vs SAC (transmission bandwidth saturation under concurrency)
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 7 (Section 5.1, explanation of Round-2 results)

evidence.claim: For DeepSeek-V3.2 serving 128K-context ShareGPT requests with 1K-token output, only 21% of the KV cache is actually utilized during decoding while the per-request KV footprint is 9.2 GB.
evidence.value: 21% KV utilization at 128K context; 9.2 GB KV per request at 128K
evidence.baseline: full prefix KV cache fetched locally
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 4 (Figure 4, Section 3.1 P2: Local Memory Wasting)

evidence.claim: Scaling the HiSparse GPU device buffer from 4K to 6K reduces the KV cache miss rate and yields an average throughput 10.4% higher, while interleaving KV cache storage across multiple CXL devices mitigates link-level contention and is projected to further close the gap to the local-DRAM baseline.
evidence.value: 6K buffer: +10.4% avg throughput vs 4K; device interleaving mitigates link contention

evaluation_context: Workload: DeepSeek-V3.2 (AWQ 4-bit quantization) end-to-end LLM serving integrated into SGLang and the HiSparse framework, context lengths 16K-128K, ShareGPT dataset (512 requests, 1K-token output). A two-round setup isolates stages: Round-1 Cache Populate (prefill instance) at concurrency 8, Round-2 Cache Hit (decode instance, prefill bypassed) at concurrency 64. Hardware topology: 8x H20 GPU server plus a 2TB CXL memory pool as KV cache backend (CXL 2.0/3.0 Type-3, cache-line-granularity load/store via CXL switch). Baselines: RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool and local host DRAM as non-disaggregated upper bound. Absolute throughput axes: Round-1 0-150 tok/s, Round-2 0-1200 tok/s; TBT axes 0-75 ms (R1) / 0-200 ms (R2); TTFT axes 0-240 s (R1) / 0-40 s (R2).
limitations: The supplement confirms the hardware setup (8x H20, 2TB CXL pool), concurrency (8 prefill / 64 decode), ShareGPT 512-request workload, and the 91%-of-DRAM throughput figure, and attributes the RDMA TBT/TTFT penalties to PCIe bus contention and transmission-bandwidth saturation respectively. However, exact absolute per-context throughput/TTFT/TBT values behind the 2.1x/9.7x/1.8x ratios are only available as figure axis ranges, not per-data-point numbers. The supplement still does not explicitly state whether the CXL fabric is CXL 3.0 hardware versus an emulator/simulator, nor the exact CXL device count (only the aggregate 2TB pool) or per-device capacity. Energy, cost-per-token and CPU utilization impact remain unquantified.
project_relevance: Directly on-topic for the memory-semantics/DSA card: SAC is a concrete case of changing the memory sharing/placement/remote-access semantics (CXL cache-line-granularity load/store replacing RDMA message semantics) and demonstrates that the fine-grained memory-semantic advantage propagates to end-to-end LLM serving throughput/TTFT/TBT for a real sparse-attention model on production-class H20 hardware. The PCIe-contention root cause for RDMA TBT and the bandwidth-saturation root cause for TTFT validate the project's question of whether micro-level memory-semantic gains conduct to end-to-end AI data-path metrics. Residual verification gap: confirm whether the CXL fabric is emulated and obtain per-context absolute latency/concurrency/CPU-utilization numbers before claiming a deployable win beyond the reported ratios.

evidence_gaps.question: Is the CXL memory pool real CXL 3.0 hardware or an emulator/simulator, and what are the absolute CXL/DRAM/RDMA read latencies (microseconds) behind the Figure 5 relative multiples?
What exact GPU model, concurrency level, batch size, and CXL device count/capacity were used for the 2.1x/9.7x/1.8x end-to-end comparison, and what are the absolute throughput, TTFT and TBT values?
